claim: Micro-fame is authority inside a category, not raw follower count; the practical variable is authority density per follower.
A high-value audience should name the creator among the most trusted people in the niche; broad but poorly matched reach can dilute that density.
The creator attributes current opportunity to zero-ramp virality, automatic targeting, and unlimited scale through recommendation feeds.
On-screen cards explicitly show '3 Core Shifts', 'Zero Ramp Virality', and 'Automatic Targeting'.
A title card names the method 'The Micro-Fame Playbook'.

Unique strategic positioning is created by finding white space across seven attributes: topic, substance depth, stories/scenarios, avatar specificity, delivery style, storytelling format, and visual format.
Crowded markets require stacking several attributes; the creator's worked example combines deeper substance, distinctive delivery, cinematic visuals, and an under-covered AI-workflow topic.
The creator reports roughly 60,000 followers in 90 days, 5.5 million views, 20,000 collected emails, and more than $100,000 revenue.
A format novelty can be cloned quickly; substance and delivery style are treated as harder-to-copy moats.
Transpositioning means learning the baseline in one's niche, then importing an effective execution pattern from a similar or distant niche instead of cloning the incumbent leader.
The video shows Sandcastles collections as a browsing surface for formats, signature series, editing styles, and visual hooks.
The 3-2-1 strategy is three topic buckets, two videos per bucket per week, and one chaos-agent post.
One bucket is broad for reach; two are narrow for avatar relevance, conversion, and trust accrual per view; the chaos agent preserves controlled exploration.
On-screen graphics state '3 2 1 Content Strategy' and spell out three topic buckets, two videos each per week, and one chaos agent.
The recommended research path is a 20-25 channel competitor set, 25K-250K followers, last three months, outlier-score sorting, minimum 2% engagement, and a 50-video initial deep-analysis batch.
The video visibly demonstrates channel discovery, sort/filter controls, analyzed-video cards, results, and CSV export inside Sandcastles.

The exported analysis is described as including transcript, topic, hook, format, and storytelling structure, then being clustered into one broad and two narrow topic buckets with personality-only outliers excluded.
The operating test is two weeks: four posts per core bucket; a bucket that underperforms across all four is killed and replaced from the candidate or chaos pool.
Strategy is only the first layer; the creator names winning-video construction, team building, evaluation, and learning transfer as subsequent operating questions.
Authority density is operationalized by balancing broad acquisition with narrow trust-building content and by pruning weak buckets, although the video does not supply a formal equation.

The seven positioning attributes form a combinatorial differentiation system: use the smallest stack that creates credible contrast and favors attributes grounded in capabilities that are difficult to copy.
